alerts.location: Dauphin
alerts.name: High Water Level
alerts.message: Manitoba's Hydrologic Forecast Centre has issued a High Water Advisory for Mossey River. Water levels are above seasonal levels and conditions may develop into a flood watch. Minor or no flooding is expected at these levels, but water may begin to overflow into nearby areas with little to no impact.
alerts.recommended: Be aware and exercise caution near waterways in the affected area. Do not attempt to cross fast flowing waters or waters of unknown depth. Avoid flooded areas. Follow directions by the local authorities. Up-to-date information is available at www.gov.mb.ca/flooding and www.manitoba511.ca or stay tuned to local media.

alerts.location: Macoun
alerts.name: Drinking Water
alerts.message: Update a Precautionary Drinking Water Advisory remains in affect for the Village of Macoun. This advisory is for the Village of Macoun and for any individuals who may access water from the Macoun water system. This advisory is in effect until further notice.
alerts.recommended: Boil water for at least 1 minute prior to use. This includes for drinking purposes, washing of fruits and vegetables and brushing teeth. Do not drink water from any public water source supplied with water from the public water supply. Use an alternative water source or RO system known to be safe. Listen for updates on the situation.

alerts.name: Yellow Advisory - Frost
alerts.message:
Freezing temperatures with frost are expected tonight.

Low temperatures will be between minus 5 and zero, depending on location. 

Temperatures will warm in the morning.

###

Damage to plants, trees, and crops is possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.
alerts.recommended: Take preventative measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees, and crops. Cover up plants, especially those in frost-prone areas.

alerts.location: Baker Lake
alerts.name: Yellow Warning - Rainfall
alerts.message:
Heavy rain is expected.

A low pressure system will bring heavy rain to communities in the Kivalliq beginning late Saturday evening and lasting through the day on Sunday. Total rainfall accumulations are expected to be between 20 and 40 mm.

Strong easterly winds coinciding with the rain are also expected, with gusts up to 90 km/h possible. This will result in visibilities being reduced at times when the rain and wind are strongest.

The rain and wind are expected to taper off Sunday evening.

###

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Local utility outages are possible.

Rainfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to rainfall amounts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.
